overall: Committee violated the OML by giving insufficient notice of its April 3 Purpose 3 session, approving CBAs without the required chair declaration, and failing to review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals; other allegations were declined or rejected.

allegations.summary: April 3 meeting notice listed a Purpose 3 collective bargaining executive session without identifying the bargaining units with which the committee was negotiating.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the bargaining units should have been identified on the meeting notice and should have been referenced in conjunction with the vote to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: March 20 meeting notice listed a conditional Purpose 3 collective bargaining executive session without identifying the bargaining unit; the committee did not convene in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law relative to the notice of the March 20 meeting.

allegations.summary: Committee approved collective bargaining agreements in executive session without the chair first declaring that an open meeting could be detrimental to its bargaining position.
allegations.key_passage: By approving collective bargaining agreements outside of public view without making the required declaration that an open meeting would have a detrimental effect on the bargaining position of the public body, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee failed to respond to requests for executive session minutes; the requests cited the Public Records Law.
allegations.key_passage: As this allegation concerns the Committee's compliance with the Public Records Law, not the Open Meeting Law, we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly did not review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals to determine whether continued nondisclosure was warranted.
allegations.key_passage: In failing to perform a review at reasonable intervals, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee allegedly relied on an improper purpose (Purpose 1) to enter executive session on May 15 to discuss an Open Meeting Law complaint.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it met in executive session to discuss an Open Meeting Law complaint.

allegations.summary: Committee waited several meetings and about six weeks to announce collective bargaining agreements reached in executive session; letter treats this as a reminder on prompt disclosure.
allegations.key_passage: Although we find no violation on this point, we remind the Committee that in the future, it should disclose the collective bargaining agreements to the public more promptly.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.

Review minutes of all executive sessions held from 2019 to present within 90 days of the letter to determine if continued non-disclosure is warranted, to the extent not reviewed in the last three months.
Recreate the missing executive session meeting minutes within 90 days of the letter to the best of its ability, using available means including attendees' memories and notes.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Law's requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
